pages.text: Profile

Full-stack developer and QTS-qualified Computer Science teacher with a First Class Honours degree in software development. Builds web applications with TypeScript, React, Next.js, Python and SQL, drawing on freelance client work and personal projects. Combines practical development with curriculum design, inclusive teaching and clear communication with non-technical users.

Profile

QTS-qualified Computer Science teacher with a First Class Honours degree and experience delivering sole Computing provision across KS3 to A Level. Previous responsibilities include curriculum redesign, assessment, examinations and inclusive teaching for students with SEND. Builds interactive education software and brings safeguarding experience, technical subject knowledge and team-management experience to teaching and curriculum leadership.
Teaching and leadership strengths
KS3–A Level Computing | Curriculum planning and assessment | Adaptive teaching and SEND support | Safeguarding and online safety | Classroom management | Interactive learning resources
Teaching experience

pages.title: Computing Teacher | Abbotsholme School
bullets: Served as the sole Computing teacher across KS3 to A Level, independently managing departmental provision without departmental support.
Redesigned the Computing curriculum, establishing a structured sequence of learning across year groups.
Developed and used an online learning-games platform covering binary, logic gates, bubble sort and search algorithms.
Applied adaptive and inclusive teaching strategies for SEND learners, including students with ASD and ADHD.
Delivered formal assessments and oversaw examinations in line with school policy and academic-integrity requirements.
Promoted safeguarding, online safety and digital wellbeing across year groups.

pages.title: Supply Teacher (Computing) | Zen Educate
bullets: Delivered Computing lessons across secondary schools in Nottingham, adapting to different school environments and student needs.
Managed classroom behaviour and supported SEND learners through adaptive teaching and one-to-one guidance.
